title: Re-attest a pending verification record after a benign binding change (claim renewal or recovery, relabel, restart, root rename) instead of treating the refusal as terminal
outcome: Preserve and settle an already registered verification record after a typed temporary lapse or missing named root, using the original immutable record and operation key after the same holder and workspace recover.
acceptance: For an already registered committed-input launcher run, a definitive current-connection Engram verification_record_refused with structured field claim_live or root_bound leaves the record pending. When the original initiating session again holds the live claim for the same work and run and the original workspace is bound, TermAl re-sends the unchanged frozen record under the original operation key and settles the resulting receipt without re-running the tests. This works across a TermAl restart when the initiating session and run artifacts survive, including a same-holder claim recovery and same-workspace name at a later generation.

TermAl keeps the existing new-registration claim and name fence and does not change the recorded work, holder, named workspace, source, result or terminal artifacts during re-attestation. Other definitive fields, invalid_request and pre-existing terminal refusals without a typed retryable field retain their final disposition. An unknown delivery outcome replays only the original request, and an already received or settled receipt is never sent again.

Behavioral tests drive the registered verification sender through both typed waits, restart and same-holder recovery, and assert the same operation key and body at the transport and one settled receipt. Negative cases show no re-send on terminal refusals, no reroute to a different session or store, no re-attestation of altered source or terminal artifacts, and no second write after a lost response to an operation Engram had already accepted.
